content_voiceover: This slide walks through the 2025 revision notes for early T precursor, or ETP, and near ETP acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The background is that outcomes for ETP ALL remained poor, and patients with a poor response often had a high MRD1 or even outright induction failure. Based on that experience, the protocol was revised in several ways around venetoclax. Venetoclax is now started earlier, during induction itself, rather than waiting. The duration of the venetoclax plus early intensification combination, abbreviated V-E-I, has been shortened. Reinduction with venetoclax, phases one and two, is now used more often. And the intensity of chemotherapy across the different phases has been adjusted accordingly to balance toxicity and efficacy. Note also that venetoclax currently requires self-payment in Taiwan, but the childhood cancer foundation now provides full subsidy. The second half of the slide defines the near ETP immunophenotype. Classic ETP still requires all four criteria to be met. Near ETP means criteria one, two, and four are satisfied, but criterion three is not, for example when CD5 is expressed at higher levels than expected. The table spells out those criteria: criterion one is an unequivocal T-ALL diagnosis with CD3 positive, CD7 positive, and myeloperoxidase negative; criterion two is CD1a negative and CD8 negative; and criterion four is expression of stem cell associated antigens like CD34, CD133, CD117, or HLA-D-R, or myeloid associated antigens like CD13, CD33, CD15, or CD11b, where just one positive marker is enough.
keypoints: ETP ALL has poor outcomes, prompting a 2025 venetoclax protocol revision
Venetoclax started earlier in induction, shorter V-E-I duration, more reinduction use
Near ETP meets criteria one, two, and four but not three, such as higher CD5
ETP diagnosis requires CD3 positive, CD7 positive, MPO negative, plus CD1a and CD8 negative
Venetoclax needs self-payment but is now fully subsidized by the childhood cancer foundation
